clue.text: Focus on coin in case

indicators.note: the coin and the word on are placed inside the case

parts.note: a crate is a packing case
taken as written
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: An instruction to stare hard at a coin lying in a display box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' reads as a display box, but it is the container; 'in' splits it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To concentrate is to fix one's attention, a verb synonym of focus.

clue.text: Some loathsome four-letter words

indicators.note: some of the letters of the next word are taken, a run lying inside it

explanation.surface: A remark that certain swear words are thoroughly nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'loathsome', after its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Four-letter words are swear words, and oaths are curses or profanities.

clue.text: Continue song and dance

explanation.surface: Go on with the singing and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to keep going; a carry-on is also a fuss or commotion, which 'song and dance' means in British idiom.

clue.text: Serve up very hot container with Mexican food

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters are written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a can is a container

explanation.surface: A chef presenting spicy Mexican food in a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve up' turns SOHCAN so it reads from the bottom of the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Nachos are tortilla chips topped with cheese, a Tex-Mex snack.

clue.text: Cocks head in outrage when lists put round

indicators.note: the lists are put round the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: rosters are duty lists

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone shaking their head in anger when rotas are circulated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head in outrage' gives O, which 'put round' places inside ROSTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocks are male fowl, and roosters are the American name for these birds.

clue.text: Starts new coffee stall after call put out

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these words, once those of the next word are taken out, are rearranged
the letters to be put out of the pool

explanation.surface: Someone opens a fresh coffee stand once the phone call is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' removes C, A, L and L from COFFEESTALL, leaving OFFEEST, which 'new' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To tee off is to begin, as a golfer starts a hole by driving from the tee.

clue.text: Confounded speed-trap plan is something on the table

indicators.note: confounded means mixed up, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A frustrated motorist cursing a police scheme to catch speeders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; the fodder is the thirteen letters of 'speed-trap plan'.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt and pepper are the condiments set out at a meal, here named in the reverse order.

clue.text: Guy in bank lacking vitality

indicators.note: the guy is placed inside the bank

parts.note: a mound is a bank of earth
to guy is to tease or mock, which is what rib means

explanation.surface: A listless man sitting in a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, but it is the verb meaning tease, and 'in' places it in the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund means near death, so stagnant and without energy.

clue.text: Tiger perhaps endlessly needing relaxation, I suspend criticism

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tiger is an example of an animal

indicators.note: to suspend is to stop or remove, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: a diversion is a pastime or relaxation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone explaining that a tiger must rest, and that they will therefore stop criticising it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' takes L from ANIMAL to give ANIMA; 'suspend' takes I from DIVERSION to give DVERSION.
explanation.definitionFit: Animadversion is a formal word for censure or a critical remark.

clue.text: Chips without fish? Come on!

indicators.note: without means the fish is removed from the word

parts.note: Chips is the traditional nickname for a ship's carpenter
a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An offer of chips with no fish, followed by an exasperated cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' suggests a takeaway, but it is naval slang for a ship's carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: To come on is to walk on, as an actor does onto a stage, the stage direction for which is the same word.

clue.text: Cease trading in neighbouring county

parts.note: close means nearby or neighbouring
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A shop shutting up in the next county.
explanation.walkthrough: DOWN is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To close down is to shut a business for good, ending its operations.

clue.text: Be careful with pet dish out

parts.note: a pussy is a pet cat
to foot a bill is to pay or dish out money

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out with the cat's food bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish out' looks like serving food, but it means pay, as in foot the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To pussyfoot is to tread warily or act timidly, avoiding commitment.

clue.text: Hate platform when power off

indicators.note: off means the letter is taken away

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Resentment on a stage when the electricity is cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is widespread hatred or disgust directed at someone.

clue.text: Embarrassed individual decorated again

parts.note: an embarrassed person turns red
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A self-conscious person whose room has been repainted.
explanation.definitionFit: Redone means done over, as a room is when it is repainted or refurbished.

clue.text: Sally behind another lady in early police visit

indicators.note: behind means the sally is placed after the other lady

parts.note: Dawn is a girl's name, another lady beside Sally
a sally is a sudden attack, a raid

explanation.surface: Sally hiding behind a second woman when the police come early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name, but it is a sortie or attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A dawn raid is a surprise police search carried out at first light.

clue.text: Very great hooker discovered

parts.note: a hooker is a prostitute, informally a pro
found means discovered

explanation.surface: A fine prostitute being uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooker' might be a rugby forward, but here it is slang for a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound means intense or deep, so very great in degree.

clue.text: Group in fine voice, abnormally high one

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: the group is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: alto is a singing voice
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A choir in good voice, one of them singing unusually high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts SET inside FALTO, after FAL; 'one' stands for a voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the artificial male voice pitched above its normal range.

clue.text: Fresh thinking is extensive in Nebraska, for instance

indicators.note: extensive goes inside the other letters

parts.note: NE is the postal abbreviation for Nebraska
as means for instance, as in such as
wide means extensive

explanation.surface: A claim that bold new thinking flourishes in Nebraska.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nebraska, for instance' looks like an example of a state, but it supplies two separate pieces; 'is' is a link and 'in' places the middle piece.
explanation.definitionFit: New ideas are original notions, which is what fresh thinking produces.

clue.text: Country house in decay, city not involved

indicators.note: the house goes inside what is left of the other word
not involved means the city is left out of the word

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London
a home is a house

explanation.surface: A rundown country house, unconnected to any city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not involved' removes the city from the decay, leaving a three-letter word, and 'in' places the house inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahomey was a West African kingdom and later nation, renamed Benin in 1975.

clue.text: Mess with honour, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals the word is as it is said, not spelt

parts.note: a medal is an honour awarded to someone

explanation.surface: A suggestion that being decorated causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to interfere or tamper with something.

clue.text: Secure magistrates on benefit? Heads to roll!

indicators.note: heads rolling means each word loses its first letter

parts.note: the bench is the body of magistrates in a court
a gain is a benefit

explanation.surface: Magistrates told to claim welfare, with sackings to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads to roll' removes the B of BENCH and the G of GAIN, leaving ENCH and AIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchain is to fasten with chains, to make secure.

clue.text: John, note, is a climber

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, a loo
fah is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A man named John, it is noted, is a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a name but is slang for a lavatory; 'climber' is a plant, not a mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: The loofah is a vine of the gourd family that climbs by tendrils.

clue.text: Lady with sex appeal gets cheer

parts.note: rah is a cheer

explanation.surface: An attractive woman being applauded.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah is a woman's name, and a crossword lady is any female name.

clue.text: Checks outside hot-air valves

indicators.note: the checks go outside, enclosing the other word

parts.note: to check is to stop
cock is British slang for nonsense or hot air

explanation.surface: Inspections outside of hot-air valves.
explanation.walkthrough: COCK means nonsense, as in 'talking cock'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopcocks are taps that regulate the flow in a pipe.

clue.text: Cold month on island such as this

definitions.text: Cold month on island such as this

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Apr is the abbreviation for April

explanation.surface: Wintry weather on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such as this' makes the whole clue point to the answer itself, an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Recurrent theme bringing Tim to life somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some unstated arrangement

explanation.surface: A theme that keeps recurring and makes Tim come alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotif is a musical phrase associated with a character, and by extension a repeated idea.

clue.text: Publicity in a post office gets agreement

indicators.note: publicity goes inside the post office

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity

explanation.surface: Advertising in a post office earns approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Appro is informal British for approval, as in goods on appro.

clue.text: City chaps on high like flattery

indicators.note: high means intoxicated, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: City men full of themselves enjoying compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks part of 'on high', but it is the anagram signal for CITYCHAPSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophantic describes fawning behaviour, using flattery to win favour.
